title: mcp_audit
description: <case>/mcp_audit.json — what an MCP server (`papertrace mcp`) records about the last audit it started in this case folder, for itself and any other server process. The audit job writes it with state `running` before the pipeline touches anything, refreshes its modification time every 15 s while it runs, and rewrites it with the outcome when it ends. A `running` record is therefore measured: refreshed within 60 s, an audit is live in some server process, and no second one is started in the folder; staler, the server writing it stopped mid-run, and the folder is not read as a result. A `failed` record keeps the folder from being read until a results.json written after it shows a later run completed the judging. Absent means no MCP server has audited this case; the CLI never writes it.

state.description: `running` while the job runs — and after, when the server stopped first, which the record's unrefreshed modification time shows. `failed`: the pipeline stopped, and what is on disk may mix that run with an earlier one.

manuscript.description: The audited PDF's absolute path — the same value audit_status gives.

started.description: When the job started: UTC, ISO 8601, to the second.

ended.description: When the job ended; null while it runs, and on an audit whose server stopped first.

error.description: Why the audit failed — the last lines the pipeline printed, or the exception's type and message. Empty unless `state` is `failed`.

scout.description: Whether this audit scanned the literature. false: any out/scout.json in the folder belongs to an earlier run, and is not served as this audit's.
